verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Gangtok until Sikkim's local demand signals and compliance position stabilise; lend only to the strongest, well-structured existing relationships.
title: Gangtok Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Gangtok-area pharma or API unit buys solvents, intermediates and packaging, runs reactors or formulation lines on power and steam, and sells to formulators or exports.** Cash is made on throughput and yield, not on price — most units are price-takers against larger Indian and Chinese suppliers. Working capital sits in inventory and receivables; API peers show working capital intensity of 52% in FY2019, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021 [9], so **assume a long cash cycle until the customer's own numbers say otherwise.** Capex is reactor-and-utility heavy and lumpy; a Cohance peer carried term loans of Rs. 152 crore with repayments back-ended from May 2025 [8].

## What has changed now
**Sikkim's local demand is contracting while India's is not.** State GST collections are -53.8% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D], and electricity demand is -0.5% against India +9.5% [D]. Nationally, output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY [D] — **credit is running far ahead of output, so pricing power is thin.** Separately, the Sikkim High Court has ordered statewide inspections of industries over waste violations [1]; so when a proposal lands, check the unit's consent-to-operate status and any inspection notice before sanctioning, and if there is an open violation, ask for the compliance plan and timeline in writing.

## Where the growth is
**Peer results are strong but they are not Gangtok.** Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [3][5]; RPG Life Sciences targets 25% API growth and is evaluating another acquisition within 12 months [4], though its stock fell over 10% after Q2 despite revenue rising 16.5% to Rs. 211.6 crore [6]. **Pursue Gangtok units that are contract-manufacturing or CDMO-linked for these larger players, with diversified customers.** Avoid single-customer units: a rated peer with Rs. 61.0 crore FY2024 revenue was flagged for high customer concentration [7]. The Governor met pharma manufacturers in Gangtok in August 2026 [2] — a relationship signal, not a demand signal.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the cash cycle, not the P&L.** Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly GST returns, and quarterly utility bills; if receivables cross the customer's stated credit terms, ask for the ageing and stop enhancement. Keep limits sized to 40-50% utilisation headroom, as the peer with Rs. 420 crore limits ran [8]. **Take a charge on receivables and inventory, and a personal guarantee on every new line.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch power and GST first.** If the unit's own electricity consumption falls while its sales grow, ask for the production log. If GST filings lag or turnover dips against the state's -53.8% [D], freeze fresh disbursal. Any new court or pollution notice [1] means stop and reassess.
watch: Two consecutive months of falling turnover -> freeze fresh disbursal and re-price
Consumption down while sales up -> demand production log and stock statement
Ageing beyond stated credit terms -> stop enhancement, seek charge enforcement
Any inspection notice or violation [1] -> halt disbursal until compliance plan is filed
